q: A high school student interested in machining looks up which math courses, certifications and degrees a community college machining program requires. She is determining:
o: academic knowledge and skills required for postsecondary education and careers
e: Know requirements before choosing a path.

q: A student who wants to become a CNC programmer should plan to build strong skills in:
o: math, blueprint reading and computer applications
e: CNC careers rely on these skills.

q: A shop manager says her customers expect parts delivered on time, to print and with a friendly response to problems. These are employer expectations that help:
A machinist who notices a defect in a finished batch before shipping should:
o: report it so it can be corrected before the customer receives it

q: A new machinist arrives early, wears the required safety gear, follows shop procedures and treats coworkers respectfully. He is demonstrating:
o: professional standards required in the workplace

q: Which habit best shows professionalism on a shop floor?
o: arriving on time and following safety procedures

q: A student writes down the certifications she wants in two years, the job she wants in five and the skills she needs to get there. She is evaluating:
A useful career goal is one that is:
o: specific and has steps and a timeline

q: When the instructions for a job are unclear, a machinist asks the supervisor to restate the part number, quantity and finish before starting. She is communicating to:
o: clarify objectives and expectations in the workplace

q: The best time to ask a question about a job's requirements is:
A machine shop requires safety glasses on the floor, labels hazardous chemicals and posts emergency exits. These practices show skills related to:
o: health and safety in the workplace as specified by OSHA

q: OSHA is the government agency that sets and enforces rules for:
A machinist writes a clear one-page procedure telling the next operator how to set up a fixture, with numbered steps and the gauge to use. She is demonstrating:
o: technical writing skills for work requirements
e: Technical writing is clear and exact.

q: Technical writing for a machine setup sheet should be:
o: clear, concise and in logical order

q: A machinist uses algebra to solve for the feed rate, geometry to find a bolt-circle position and trigonometry to find an angled cut. He is demonstrating:
o: mathematical skills such as algebra, geometry and trigonometry
e: Machining uses several kinds of math.

q: A bolt circle of four holes is laid out on a plate. The angle between adjacent holes is:
A machinist reads a print with feature control frames that show flatness, perpendicularity and position tolerances for each surface. She is interpreting:
o: engineering drawings, including those with geometric dimensioning and tolerancing
e: GD&T defines form and position tolerances.

q: On a print, a feature control frame tells the machinist:
o: the geometric tolerance that applies to a feature
e: It specifies form, orientation or location.

q: A student looks at a print that shows a part from the front, top and right side and then at a picture that shows all three faces in one angled view. She is describing:
o: orthographic and isometric views of three-dimensional figures
e: Ortho = separate views; iso = one 3D view.

q: A single drawing that shows the top, front and right faces of a part at once is called an:
A machinist calculates the spindle speed for a 0.500-inch end mill cutting aluminum and checks that the answer is reasonable. She is evaluating:
o: mathematics as it applies to precision machining operations

q: Spindle speed (RPM) for a cutter is found by:
A machinist notes that cutting with a dull tool produces more heat and needs more force because of friction. He is discussing basic concepts of physics, such as:
o: friction, force and heat as applied to machining

q: The heat generated while cutting metal is mostly carried away by:
o: the chips and the cutting fluid
e: Chips remove most of the heat.

q: A student looks up a thread's pitch diameter in the handbook, checks a catalog for a recommended insert grade and a speeds-and-feeds app for a chart. She is examining:
o: resources found in recognized manufacturing reference materials

q: A reliable reference for the dimensions of standard threads is:
A machinist uses a chart to find that a 1/4-20 tap needs a #7 drill. He is demonstrating knowledge of:
o: the uses of reference charts such as tap drill charts
e: Tap drill charts list drill sizes.

q: A tap drill chart tells a machinist:
o: what drill size to use before tapping a thread
e: The chart matches drill to tap.

q: A student checks that guards are in place on a lathe, ties back long hair and keeps the chuck key out of the chuck before starting. She is practicing:
o: safety while running equipment commonly employed in machine shops

q: A chuck key should never be left in the chuck because it:
o: can be thrown out at high speed when the spindle starts

q: A student sorts used coolant, oily rags and spent solvent into labeled containers instead of the regular trash. She is:
o: identifying and properly disposing of environmentally hazardous materials

q: Used oily rags in a machine shop should be placed in:
o: a plastic bag in the trash
an approved, closed metal safety can

q: A class loads a G-code program into a small CNC mill, sets the work offset and runs it in single-block mode to watch each move. They are demonstrating knowledge of:
Running a new CNC program in single-block mode lets the operator:
A student reports on how 5-axis machining, automated tool changers and in-process probing may change what machinists do. She is demonstrating knowledge of:
o: emerging technologies that may affect the machining industry

q: A probe mounted in a CNC spindle can:
o: measure a part on the machine

q: A shop heats a steel tool to a high temperature and quenches it to make it hard, then reheats it to a lower temperature to reduce brittleness. These steps are:
After hardening, steel is often tempered to:
A student practices setting up a vise on a mill and writes up the process for a job-shadow with a local machine shop. She is applying:
o: technical knowledge and skills in a machine shop to career preparation
e: Skills are applied in a career setting.

q: A job-shadow day at a machine shop helps a student by:
o: showing real working conditions and skills employers want

q: A class sorts samples into steel, aluminum, brass and plastics such as nylon and acetal and notes how each cuts. They are identifying:
Of these, a non-metallic material often machined in a shop is:
A student compares the type, structure, bond and typical use of aluminum oxide and silicon carbide wheels. She is comparing:
e: Abrasives differ in type and use.

q: An aluminum oxide wheel is generally used to grind:
A student puts on safety glasses, secures a part in a vise and clears the bench before filing and layout. She is using:
o: equipment commonly employed in bench work and layout in a safe manner

q: When using a hand file, the safe practice is to:
o: push it with a bare tang
use a handle on the tang

q: A student files a steel block flat, then files a 30-degree angle on one end and a radius on a corner to match a template. She is developing the ability to:
o: use a file to cut flats, angles and radiuses

q: To keep a file cutting well, a worker should:
o: clean the teeth with a file card

q: A student coats a part with layout dye, then uses a height gage and a scriber to mark lines from a drawing onto the metal. She is employing:
o: standard layout tools to transfer a part design to the actual piece

q: Layout dye is applied to a metal surface so that:
o: scribed lines are easy to see

q: A student marks hole locations with a center punch, then drills each hole with a handheld drill. She is performing:
o: center punching and hand drilling of holes using an electric or air drill

q: A center punch mark is made before drilling in order to:
A student drills a 0.201-inch hole and then turns a 1/4-20 tap a half turn forward and a quarter turn back to cut internal threads. She is performing:
When hand tapping, turning the tap back a little after each forward turn:
o: breaks the chip so it does not jam

q: A student runs a straight reamer through a drilled hole with a drill to finish it to an exact size. She is performing:
o: hand reaming of holes using an electric or air hand drill

q: A hole is reamed after drilling to:
o: change its shape to a square
improve its size and surface finish

q: A student works from a print to lay out every hole and edge of a NIMS-style practice part and checks the layout against a gauge. She is developing:
o: a detailed layout part such as the NIMS Level 1 layout project

q: The National Institute for Metalworking Skills (NIMS) sets:
o: industry-recognized standards and credentials for metalworking

q: A student completes a NIMS-style bench part by filing, drilling, reaming and tapping to the dimensions on the print. She is developing:
o: a detailed bench work part such as the NIMS Level 1 bench work project

q: Before declaring a bench work part complete, the student should:
o: inspect it against the print dimensions

q: At the end of each class, a student sweeps chips, wipes the benches, puts tools back in their cabinet and wipes up coolant spills. She is employing:
o: basic housekeeping skills in a machine shop

q: A clean, organized shop floor helps prevent:
A student wipes a micrometer's anvil and spindle faces, zeros it and handles it without dropping it before measuring a shaft. She is using:
o: equipment commonly used in precision measurement in a safe manner

q: A micrometer should be stored with its measuring faces:
A quality technician lists the features to be checked on a bracket, the tool for each, the tolerance and how many parts to sample. She is writing:
e: An inspection plan defines what to measure.

q: An inspection plan for a machined part should list:
o: the features, tolerances and measuring tools

q: To check a hole that must be 0.500 inch plus or minus 0.001 inch, a technician picks a bore gage rather than a ruler. She is identifying and selecting:
o: the required measuring instruments to conduct the inspection

q: A good rule is that a measuring instrument should be at least how many times more precise than the tolerance being checked?
A shop plots the diameter of every tenth part on a chart with upper and lower limits to see when the process starts drifting. She is describing:
The purpose of statistical process control is to:
o: detect process changes before bad parts are made

q: A student uses a tool post, a tailstock and a steady rest to hold and support a long shaft in the lathe. She is using:
o: accessories commonly implemented on and around a lathe in a safe manner

q: A steady rest is used on a lathe to:
A student weighs the slower setup and the ability to center odd-shaped parts of a four-jaw chuck against the speed of a three-jaw chuck. She is analyzing:
o: the advantages and disadvantages of a four-jaw independent chuck and a three-jaw chuck

q: A four-jaw independent chuck is the better choice for holding:
o: square or irregular parts that must be centered precisely

q: A student sets a dial indicator on a part in a four-jaw chuck and adjusts the jaws until the needle moves no more than 0.003 inch total. She is:
o: indicating a part in a four-jaw independent chuck within .003 inch total indicator reading

q: TIR on a dial indicator stands for:
A student labels the headstock, tailstock, carriage, cross slide, compound rest and spindle on a drawing of a lathe. She is identifying and describing:
The part of a lathe that holds the cutting tool and moves along the bed is the:
A student picks a live center, a drill chuck, a boring bar and a knurling tool for different lathe jobs. She is identifying and using:
o: accessories and tooling for turning operations

q: A knurling tool on a lathe is used to:
o: press a textured pattern into a part for grip

q: A student bores a hole to size, chamfers the edge, cuts a 1/2-13 thread and parts off the finished piece. She is demonstrating:
o: standard turning operations such as boring, chamfering, cutting threads and parting

q: Parting on a lathe means:
o: cutting a finished piece off the stock

q: A student lists the steps, tools, speeds, feeds and depths of cut that will be used to turn a stepped shaft, in order. She is writing:
o: a detailed process plan for turning

q: A good process plan for turning lists the operations:
o: in the sequence they will be performed

q: A student turns a chuck-style practice part with several diameters, a thread and a groove to NIMS-style print dimensions. She is developing:
o: a detailed turning part such as the NIMS Level 1 turning project

q: After turning a part, a student checks that it meets the print by:
o: measuring each dimension with the right gauge

q: After each class a student cleans the chips from the ways, wipes down the machine and puts a few drops of way oil on the slides. She is employing:
o: basic preventative maintenance on the lathe

q: Lubricating the ways of a lathe regularly helps to:
o: reduce wear and keep movement smooth

q: A student clamps a part in a vise, wears safety glasses and keeps hands away from the cutter while a mill runs. She is using:
o: equipment commonly used with a milling machine in a safe manner

q: Chips from a milling machine should be cleared with:
o: a brush or a chip hook, not bare hands
a rag while the machine runs

q: A student compares clamping a plate directly to the table, using a vise and using a fixture plate, noting the setup time and accuracy of each. She is analyzing:
o: the advantages and disadvantages of various work holding methods

q: A milling vise is best for holding:
o: small to medium parts with parallel sides

q: A student contrasts the roles of an end mill holder, a boring head, a rotary table and a dividing head. She is contrasting:
o: various ancillary tools used on milling machines

q: A rotary table on a milling machine is used to:
e: Rotary tables index and rotate work.

q: A student identifies the column, knee, saddle, table, quill and spindle on a diagram of a vertical mill. She is identifying:
o: the components of a milling machine and their functions

q: The component of a vertical mill that holds the cutter and rotates is the:
A student uses a dial test indicator on the spindle and adjusts the head until the reading is the same at two points across the table. She is:
o: tramming in the head of a vertical milling machine

q: A mill head is trammed so that:
o: the spindle is square to the table

q: A student sets a workpiece in a milling vise, taps it down on parallels and checks the face with a dial indicator before cutting. She is:
o: locating and setting a workpiece in a milling vise using a dial indicator

q: A reason to indicate a part in a vise is to:
o: confirm it is square and positioned correctly

q: A student mills all six faces of an aluminum block so that opposite faces are parallel and adjacent faces are square, to within a few thousandths. She is developing:
o: a square block in the milling machine to close tolerances

q: After milling a block square, the student checks that adjacent faces are square by using:
A student spot drills, drills, reams and counterbores holes in a plate at coordinates from the print. She is demonstrating:
o: various hole-making activities such as spot drilling, drilling, reaming and boring

q: A spot drill is used before a twist drill in order to:
A student takes a cut with the cutter turning against the feed and then with it, and mills a slot and a pocket in an aluminum plate. She is demonstrating:
o: various milling activities such as climb milling, conventional milling, slotting and pocketing

q: In climb milling, the cutter teeth rotate:
o: with the direction of the feed
e: Climb milling cuts with the feed.

q: A student writes the sequence of operations for milling a bracket, including the cutter size, speeds, feeds and depth of cut for each pass. She is writing:
o: a detailed process plan for milling, including feeds, speeds and tooling

q: A process plan for a mill job should include the:
o: tools, speeds, feeds and order of operations

q: A student mills a practice part with pockets, slots, holes and a contour to NIMS-style dimensions. She is developing:
o: a detailed milling part such as the NIMS Level 1 milling part

q: Before removing a milled part from the vise, a good habit is to:
o: check that critical features are within tolerance

q: After a mill job, a student brushes the chips off the table, wipes the machine, checks the coolant level and oils the ways. She is employing:
o: basic preventative maintenance on the milling machine

q: Keeping a mill's table and ways clean and lubricated helps to:
o: prevent wear and keep it accurate

q: Before running a surface grinder, a student checks the wheel for cracks, stands to the side during the first start-up and wears eye protection. She is using:
o: proper safety procedures for surface grinding operations

q: A new grinding wheel should be started up:
o: with guards in place and the operator out of line with the wheel

q: A student uses a band saw, a pedestal grinder and a drill press, following the posted rules for each. She is using:
o: support equipment commonly found in a machine shop in a safe manner

q: Before using the pedestal grinder, a worker should:
o: adjust the tool rest close to the wheel

q: A student picks a grinding wheel for sharpening a drill bit, checking the grit, grade and the rated speed against the grinder's RPM. She understands:
o: basic pedestal grinder functions such as wheel selection

q: A grinding wheel should never be used at a speed greater than:
A student chooses a blade with the right tooth count, sets the band saw's speed for aluminum and adjusts the feed. She understands:
o: basic sawing functions such as band type, speed and feeds

q: For cutting thin material on a band saw, the best blade has:
A student clamps a part to the table, centers the drill using a center punch and selects the correct speed for the drill size and material. She understands:
o: basic drill press operations, including work holding and speeds

q: On a drill press, the larger the drill bit, generally:
o: the slower the speed should be
